title: Bosnia Holds Elections as Leader Declares Victory for His Party
summary:
Voters in Bosnia and Herzegovina chose their leaders on Sunday. The election was shaped by money worries, the country's hopes of joining the European Union, and divisions between ethnic groups. These divisions date back to a war in the early 1990s.

Milorad Dodik is a Bosnian Serb nationalist politician. He declared victory for his party. He was not on the ballot. He was banned from public office after being convicted last year of defying decisions by the official who oversees the 1995 peace agreement. Even so, he was central to the campaign.

With nearly 90 percent of votes counted, Dodik's ally Zeljka Cvijanovic had more than 55 percent for the Serb seat on the three-member presidency. Dodik gave credit to U.S. President Donald Trump's 2024 election win and to Russian President Vladimir Putin's support. "No one should ask us to change our politics," he said.

Other candidates also claimed victory before counting was finished. Around 3.4 million people could vote. These are not final results.
why_it_matters: Bosnia's leaders are chosen by a system built after a war, so this vote shows how the country is dealing with old divisions and its hopes of joining the European Union.
